newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech flood damage estimated at CZK 60 bln-agency.
newsitem.headline: Czech flood damage estimated at CZK 60 bln-agency.

text.p: A special Czech government crisis team has estimated total damage from floods which devastated areas in the eastern section of the country last month at 60 billion crowns ($1.8 billion), the Czech news agency CTK reported on Monday.

It quoted environmental minister Jiri Skalicky who heads the team as saying that the estimate was made from an expert analysis of individual ministries and district offices from the afflicted area. Previous estimates had put the total at 50 to 100 billion crowns. ($ = 34.04 Czech Crowns)

The huge floodwaters which swept through Central Europe after torrential rains in early July were responsible for more than 100 deaths in Poland and the Czech Republic and caused extensive damage on both sides of the Polish border with Germany.
The floods destroyed thousands of homes, businesses and crops, costing billions of dollars throughout the region.
The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) has said the flooding would mean that Czech economic growth for the year would be at the low end of its 2.0 to 3.0 percent range.
But Ivan Sujan, vice-chairman of the CSU, told CTK that his personal estimate was for growth of only 1.5 to 2.0 percent.
